body:
Participation is the name of the game. Everything we do is with an eye towards to activating and turning out more voters, no matter which method they choose to vote.
RUSH $25 or more right now to help us drive an avalanche of voter participation in next year's critical midterm elections >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-infrastructure?refcode=102925_3&amount=25]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
folks,
Voting isn't a "one size fits all" activity. Forcing one method of participation only drives potential voters away, which is why we support a "yes, and" approach to casting your ballot. Here's how this works:
Can someone vote in person on Election Day? Yes, and they can also complete a ballot at home and mail it back. Are there other ways to participate? Yes, and they can drop that home ballot in a secure drop box, and they could vote early instead, and we can make Election Day a holiday to free more people to go vote... you get the idea. Simply put, the more ways we can make it easy for voters to participate, the more people who will make their voice heard by voting.
One of those methods -- early voting -- is open in many states with elections coming up. When Americans vote early, they ensure that nothing – not last minute problems, confusing election laws, long lines, or voter disinformation – can stop us from voting and making our voice heard.
Our mission is simple: The more people who vote, the more our government looks like what we, the people, want it to be. But to reach these voters and get them involved, we need your help .
Will you continue to fuel our work with $25 or whatever you can today to help us reach every voter we can ahead of their next election? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-infrastructure?refcode=102925_3&amount=25]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-infrastructure?express_lane=true&refcode=102925_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-infrastructure?express_lane=true&refcode=102925_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-infrastructure?express_lane=true&refcode=102925_3&amount=50]

Want to learn more about early voting? Our partners at Vote Early Day [https://voteearlyday.org/] have tool kits and information for you to help in your community. We've also got a full suite of Voter Tools on our website [https://voteractionproject.org/voter-tools/] to help you get ready to vote in your next election.
Whether you vote by mail, drop your ballot in a drop box, vote early, or vote on Election Day, we must make sure everyone turns out and all our voices are heard. Chip in again with $25 or whatever you can today to make sure every voter turns out and every vote counts >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-infrastructure?refcode=102925_3&amount=25]
Thank you,
Voter Action Project's Turnout Team
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
https://www.facebook.com/voteraction [https://www.facebook.com/voteraction] https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org [https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org] https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/ [https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/] https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/ [https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/]
Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

| | | | | |
**Team Mackenzie,****We need your help!** Right now, **Chuck Schumer and Senate Democrats** continue to play political games with people’s livelihoods — hurting the most vulnerable Pennsylvanians through what’s become known as the **Schumer Shutdown**.At the same time, crucial **2025 local elections are just days away** and every volunteer, every door knocked, and every conversation matters.

We’re not standing by for either. We’re stepping up - and hope you can join us this weekend for **two very important efforts:**
* * *

### **🚪 1. Northampton County Door-Knocking Launch**
**When:** Saturday, November 1st at 11:00 AM
**Where:** Northampton County GOP Office, 2523 Willow Park Rd, Bethlehem, PAJoin us as we go door-to-door supporting our **local 2025 candidates** in the final push before Election Day. You’ll be paired with a team and given all the materials you need to help get out the vote and share why these races matter for our communities.
---
|
---
| |

### **🥫 2. Mackenzie Team Food Drive**
**When:** Saturday, November 1st, 1:30–3:30 PM
**Where:** Mackenzie Campaign HQ, 1125 S Cedar Crest Blvd, Suite 106, Allentown, PA 18103With SNAP and WIC benefits set to expire Friday due to the Schumer Shutdown, local food banks—already stretched thin—are about to face even greater strain. **Enough is enough.** We’re taking action. As Republicans, and more importantly as Americans, we’re coming together to help those in need. Congressman Mackenzie and our team will be hosting a **community food drive** to support local food banks impacted by the shutdown.Bring a **non-perishable food donation** , or volunteer to help sort and pack items. Every bit helps.

* * *

### **Donations Needed**
* Canned goods (soup, vegetables, fruit, tuna, chicken, etc.)
* Pasta, rice, tomato sauce
* Cereal, oatmeal, granola bars, snack packs
* Baby diapers & formula
* Canned spaghetti meals (Chef Boyardee, Spaghetti-O’s)
* Evaporated or powdered milk
* Personal hygiene items: soap, shampoo, toothpaste, toothbrushes, deodorant, feminine hygiene products

---
|
---
| | This weekend is about more than politics — it’s about **standing together** to help our neighbors and defend our values.Let’s show what Team Mackenzie stands for: **service, community, and leadership for working families.** See you Saturday!**– Ryan Mackenzie**

subject: 48 hours to shape the next generation of leaders
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
What happens next Tuesday — and in the next 48 hours — will echo for years to come.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20251029-1&t=1&akid=2786%2E587540%2EZX3zmT)
Peter,
Time is running out. We only have 48 hours to meet our end-of-month fundraising goal and help some of our endorsed candidates win next Tuesday.
But this isn’t just about hitting a deadline or next week’s elections. This is about a **moment that will shape the next election cycle, the next decade, and who the next generation of leaders will be.**
**[Please chip in $5 right now to help us hit our goal, win next week’s races, and make a long-term investment in progressive, young leadership.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251029_1_investment.JLTSjq&refcode=em20251029-2786&amount=5&t=3&akid=2786%2E587540%2EZX3zmT)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251029_1_investment.JLTSjq&amount=5&refcode=em20251029-2786&t=4&akid=2786%2E587540%2EZX3zmT)**
**Time is one of the most valuable assets in politics — and young people have it.** Lincoln, Obama, AOC, and countless others all started young. **Just imagine the leaders of tomorrow that we’re electing together today.**
When we say young people are the future, we mean it — and we mean it _strategically._ We’re not asking you to support our endorsed candidates just because they’re young. We’re asking you to make a _long-term, early investment_ in the very leaders who will be at the forefront of fighting for climate action, affordable healthcare, gun control, and so much more. These issues will last for decades. So, we can’t settle for the same complacent politicians that got us into this mess. We must ensure bold, progressive leaders who can fight for the long haul are in charge.
And that starts with supporting great people when they are young, empowering them with the skills to lead for decades to come. People like Christian Menefee and Akbar Ali, two inspiring young leaders who are both on the ballot next week. And leaders like Zohran Mamdani, who is inspiring a progressive movement to bring positive change to New York City with free childcare, fast buses and more.
And that’s just the start. These are the same leaders who could run for Senate or the White House one day, but only if we support them right now.
We don’t take corporate PAC money. Neither do our candidates. **We are 100% powered by grassroots support from folks like you (that is why you get so many emails from me, by the way. I really do appreciate you reading this far!).**
We need to close our end-of-month fundraising gap by midnight this Friday to give our candidates on the ballot next week — and the ones who will lead for generations to come — the resources to win.
**[Please contribute $5 now to help us cross the finish line and power the next generation of leaders.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251029_1_investment.JLTSjq&amount=5&refcode=em20251029-2786&t=5&akid=2786%2E587540%2EZX3zmT)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251029_1_investment.JLTSjq&amount=5&refcode=em20251029-2786&t=24&akid=2786%2E587540%2EZX3zmT)**
The more leaders we elect today, the stronger our bench is for tomorrow.
Thank you for your support.
— David Hogg

body:
THE GARAND

Introducing The Garand — a limited-release salute to American grit and battlefield glory from Patriot Cigar Company.

Hand-rolled in a commanding 7.5 x 48 Churchill, The Garand stands tall like the legendary rifle it’s named after — a symbol of strength, precision, and American might. Expertly crafted with 7-year aged Nicaraguan tobacco and finished in a rich Habano wrapper, this cigar delivers a smooth, medium-strength profile that fires off bold flavor with every draw — steady, confident, and unmistakably patriotic.

AVAILABLE IN 5 PACKS ONLY!
https://mypatriotcigars.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3ea77f33fc36dd7515163e71c&id=985c2cc645&e=fbf55fa623

This is a STRICTLY limited release.
When The Garand is gone — it’s gone. No restock. No second run.

Lock, load, and light up history.

About The Garand

The Garand from Patriot Cigar Company is more than a premium hand-rolled cigar — it is a cigar built in tribute to the rifle that helped secure victory for freedom across the world: the M1 Garand, the rifle General George S. Patton famously called “the greatest battle implement ever devised.”

A commanding 7.5 x 48 Churchill, The Garand is rolled with precision and reverence, echoing the engineering excellence of its namesake. Packed with 7-year aged Nicaraguan filler and binder, and clad in a beautifully finished Habano wrapper, this cigar offers a confidently smooth medium-strength profile — a slow-burning, dignified smoke with depth, refinement, and authority. It is rich without being overpowering, balanced yet bold, a cigar built for those who honor legacy as much as flavor.
------------------------------------------------------------

** A Tribute to a Legend
------------------------------------------------------------

Adopted by the U.S. military in 1936 and carried proudly through World War II and the Korean War, the M1 Garand was the first standard-issue semi-automatic battle rifle in the world — a game-changer in combat. Where other nations’ soldiers still chambered rounds by hand, American troops were able to fire shot after shot with speed and reliability. It was rugged. It was accurate. It was trusted in the mud, the snow, the jungles, and the beaches of Normandy. It represented innovation, confidence, and overwhelming American firepower.

The M1 Garand wasn’t just a rifle — it was a handheld symbol of American dominance and ingenuity, a lifeline to soldiers whose courage reshaped history.
------------------------------------------------------------

** The Cigar Worthy of the Name
------------------------------------------------------------

The spirit of that legendary rifle lives in this limited-edition release:
* 7.5 x 48 Churchill — a proud, commanding presence
* 7-year aged Nicaraguan tobacco — matured for depth and character
* Habano wrapper — warm, rich, and worthy of a namesake of warfighters
* Medium strength — a long, thoughtful smoke that marches forward with confidence

This cigar is meant to be enjoyed the way history is remembered — deliberately, with pride, and without rush.
------------------------------------------------------------

** A One-Time Tribute
------------------------------------------------------------

Like the heroes who carried the M1 across the world, The Garand will not be mass-produced or remade. This is a strictly limited release — when this cigar is gone, it’s gone. No second run. No encore.

Light one in honor of the warriors who stood between tyranny and liberty — and for the enduring American spirit that still refuses to yield.

The Garand
A rifle that won wars.
A cigar that honors the warrior.

Hand-rolled in a commanding 7.5 x 48 Churchill, The Garand stands tall like the legendary rifle it’s named after — a symbol of strength, precision, and American might. Expertly crafted with 7-year aged Nicaraguan tobacco and finished in a rich Habano wrapper, this cigar delivers a smooth, medium-strength profile that fires off bold flavor with every draw — steady, confident, and unmistakably patriotic. AVAILABLE IN 5 PACKS ONLY! This is a STRICTLY limited release. When The Garand is gone — it’s gone. No restock. No second run. Lock, load, and light up history. About The Garand The Garand from Patriot Cigar Company is more than a premium hand-rolled cigar — it is a cigar built in tribute to the rifle that helped secure victory for freedom across the world: the M1 Garand, the rifle General George S. Patton famously called “the greatest battle implement ever devised.” A commanding 7.5 x 48 Churchill, The Garand is rolled with precision and reverence, echoing the engineering excellence of its namesake. Packed with 7-year aged Nicaraguan filler and binder, and clad in a beautifully finished Habano wrapper, this cigar offers a confidently smooth medium-strength profile — a slow-burning, dignified smoke with depth, refinement, and authority. It is rich without being overpowering, balanced yet bold, a cigar built for those who honor legacy as much as flavor. A Tribute to a Legend Adopted by the U.S. military in 1936 and carried proudly through World War II and the Korean War, the M1 Garand was the first standard-issue semi-automatic battle rifle in the world — a game-changer in combat. Where other nations’ soldiers still chambered rounds by hand, American troops were able to fire shot after shot with speed and reliability. It was rugged. It was accurate. It was trusted in the mud, the snow, the jungles, and the beaches of Normandy. It represented innovation, confidence, and overwhelming American firepower. The M1 Garand wasn’t just a rifle — it was a handheld symbol of American dominance and ingenuity, a lifeline to soldiers whose courage reshaped history. A One-Time Tribute Like the heroes who carried the M1 across the world, The Garand will not be mass-produced or remade. This is a strictly limited release — when this cigar is gone, it’s gone. ## Fed Cuts Rates Again Amid Job Worries
The Federal Reserve cut [interest rates by a quarter point](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAQhp8Gb0QH2I4zMHTxlq4dLTBHQoTBhXMsv33lSn2Cbied9P3_93_dp7sJMaTHp1lQk89Twr1GJMIyhURYsFIxhPNGNm74MkfdwyRBdlwAVzA5E-IxtY3THlGialCLay8GMfRKNU-NAIgCexhsBx0IB_6K1go7D84raZqgT5oABQJAdfLSKuXdbXAGOiFu2LMW0AXK5fLKIdETfTzyG8tlzksT9ZNorUx9MDkyOaZjzZXOF5PjCWZyFHDeNyZHu9WQsFYmR4-OzxtV_mfJT83K7cG_N1MIC1_POO5z4RXnnBynsCAPiRte8s7k2BTt1j3EGGp_ZS08FhPiby3615ZvLX8CAAD__yq7iPk) Wednesday, marking its second straight reduction as job growth continues to slow. Rates now sit between 3.75% and 4%, the lowest since 2022, though Chair Jerome Powell warned another cut in [December is far from a foregone conclusion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OgzAQhJ_GdCD_gaFwcQ1drr0SGe8SNjI4MpugvP2Je4XrRprRN5r5uU23QIn2-3fY0POSpx3PIyEzlol2xoIHl8AYXzynFz7C5zhp0lK3tZK1kRMESp_JVuAXRI2mQq9cp3rVd8ZUq9cz2KDcEMCBmyNEdJ2zvZUSoe9cW5G_aEoaqaQ0rW6sMQsMPQTZKjVgJ6xEIM6leWTaecUlffIbSxPzViW_Mj8PYb6EHoUez_Ns4j7HyxR6vNBCj0peehB6XBDqa08NGOmgvNc5cp6x1Fe0WXlLVfHwPCklOjonrLxvgdJfGf_robfXvwEAAP__LZF4aQ). In September, officials predicted rate cuts in both October and December. But Powell signaled that the government shutdown, which has halted economic data, could thwart the plan. Wednesday's decision split policymakers, with Trump-appointed Fed board member Stephen Miran pushing for a deeper cut and [Kansas City’s Jeffrey Schmid](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O6yAURlcDHdHlz9gFxWvc5bVTWsRcYiJiR3CdyLsfeaRZwdTfpyOd83WdriGXvN7_hyd6Stu04qcVJMI65ZWwYqMaCOedbmXHRzjaJ08KlBUShIYphlyOyfDoE6JCzdFL18le9p3WfPHSWueCNjFFOcMAadCzhGSMHdzsXOLZnzQJGiSAtupitE5x6GMAK-WAHTOAMdNWL48tr7RgKsf2xnqZtycvfiF6Nab_MTUyNdKCSy7l3Jgab3vLK7bG1GitG1QPImHEGoqo2LC-Ucw7NfFrKk7V882rj69PLiW3zjED92fIP1BOf6r09uo7AAD__8rMe8w) opposing any change.
## Melissa Slams Eastern Cuba
Hurricane Melissa made [landfall near Chivirico, Cuba](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuOszAQhZ_GdI58AUIKF39Dl7_dEk3sITg72JE9BPH2K_YVtjvSkb5z-bpPd4gU0_M_rOh4zlPCvRIyY5liYixYuQCj3_hBG77gqHucjDKd1EpaNQWIdExtE9yMaNA26PS114MeemubxVk9DNqg9zCYDq4Y2l51EED3Q49Wmya6k6aVVVop25lLa-0cbkMA1Wl9w160CkPkXC6vHBMvONORP1guPq8NuYX5XYX9J8wozJiOd658WsKMJ1iYUatT34QZ91woyHOiMOOylRI9JJQrUqwV5ArfWCVBCjMQyZgkQmUsSfrtARKqBOmB8ZnLIa2snMsZ0xQX3nskirW_ilY9V4j0247_dOnHmZ8AAAD__w-4ipk), early Wednesday as a Category 3 storm with 120 mph winds, after tearing through Jamaica with near-record intensity. At least 25 people have been killed in Haiti alone as the storm triggered widespread flooding, power outages, and landslides. [See the hurricane forecast here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQRp8Gd0Qw-CcuKLZxl223tMZmiInARDCOlbdfZVf3vsCtj_TpO-fPbb5hiGG__8ZEln2edzprJGYqc9iZClUuyLQevMSDHviuZ5hBQSe1kkbNDkN8z23jrCcCMg1ZPfT6qq-9Mc1mqV0I3ODRkx_HBWD0vUbtoaOug8E1wX7WtDJKK2U6uLTGeDdeHapO65F60SpygXO5PHLYeSMf3_lF5bLm1ES7MT-rML8ETAKmk5C3_0zAVDmXVAVM21FKWHEnAdPHUMD05QCj_KYyUQy1ovS50IqV5YIbJqxyoZIOh_KBCcOKcj0WbIp1zzPEGGo_iFbdE4b47xX_KOXLwt8AAAD__6epiek). Cuba evacuated hundreds of thousands ahead of the storm, which is now expected to move into the Bahamas. ## Ranking: Average Cost of Electricity by State
New data from 2025 reveal [significant variation in electricity rates](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OozAQAJ8GOiP_AA6Fi2vocu2VaGMvYSODkb2AePtTvlf4-tGMNP-e0xMo0vb-Cys6ntO04VUiMmOeaGPMWDgDoz_4FQ_8wF0umrTUnVBSGDkFoHhPbR3cjKjR1OiU7dVDPXpj6sV539lg-zArazvjB9AwGGs7aUPoO481ua9NSSOVlKbTTWvMHIZHANkpNWBftRIDccrNJ9HGC87xTifmxqe1jm5h3ktl_lR6rPR4XVdzUjkgetiJIVLhL1jpcYV9xyB4QQEnZnij8KmwSLPAiJ4zeeJbvG5xiCIKA2Olxzq7sF8UI5XeVq18r0DxJ82_-nU6_T8AAP__IjiBYg) across the United States, with Hawaii recording the highest average prices: 40.96¢ per kWh for residential customers and 35.54¢ for commercial users. California follows at 33.52¢ and 26.69¢, respectively, with Massachusetts, New York, and Alaska also ranking among the most expensive states. In contrast, Nevada (10.11¢), Idaho (10.54¢), and North Dakota (10.87¢) report the lowest average rates, driven by access to local energy resources and lower transmission costs. Texas stands out for its wide price gap between residential (15.23¢) and commercial (8.60¢) customers, reflecting the state’s deregulated energy market. See [where your state ranks here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OozAQAJ8GOiP_AA6Fi2vocu2VaGMvYSODkb2AePtTvlf4-tGMNP-e0xMo0vb-Cys6ntO04VUiMmOeaGPMWDgDoz_4FQ_8wF0umrTUnVBSGDkFoHhPbR3cjKjR1OiU7dVDPXpj6sV539lg-zArazvjB9AwGGs7aUPoO481ua9NSSOVlKbTTWvMHIZHANkpNWBftRIDccrNJ9HGC87xTifmxqe1jm5h3ktl_lR6rPR4XVdzUjkgetiJIVLhL1jpcYV9xyB4QQEnZnij8KmwSLPAiJ4zeeJbvG5xiCIKA2Olxzq7sF8UI5XeVq18r0DxJ82_-nU6_T8AAP__IjiBYg).

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. Hey folks, it's Cliff.
Chris Peleo-Lazar--Chris Matthews' producer guest hosting--invited me on the big show.
It was a bit surreal seeing a guy whose papers I once graded (during those heady days working on my American History PhD, which became ABD) tossing me _Hardball_ -style questions on live TV. (Don't worry, Chris--you were reasonable enough you get to keep the A-minus.)
We dove right into the meat of it: how the Democratic Party lost its appetite for a good fight. I talked about the new **Roosevelt Institute report** , which lays it out plain--Democrats became the "steady-as-she-goes" party while Republicans went full demolition derby on the rule of law.
[My message? ](https://substack.com/redirect/af35850b-85a2-44e0-a013-306ef0cc4ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Have the damn fight.](https://substack.com/redirect/af35850b-85a2-44e0-a013-306ef0cc4ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ Stop treating Mitch McConnell like he's a disappointed headmaster.](https://substack.com/redirect/af35850b-85a2-44e0-a013-306ef0cc4ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) The filibuster isn't scripture; it's a relic that keeps progress hostage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/af35850b-85a2-44e0-a013-306ef0cc4ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

We talked about **Project 2025** --Trump's little fascist starter kit--and [how Democrats need an FDR-sized spine to counter it](https://substack.com/redirect/af35850b-85a2-44e0-a013-306ef0cc4ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). FDR didn't whine about the courts; he stared them down until they blinked.
That's the model. Build new institutions, break up monopolies, and remind working people that government can still be a force for good.
I may have gotten a little animated--shocking, I know--when we hit the billionaire beat.
Because while regular Americans are juggling rent and childcare, the ultra-rich are playing "cyborg wedding Barbie" with 50-million-dollar ceremonies. It's grotesque, and why both _populism_ and _fighting_ billionaire-owned Republicans aren't dirty words for Democrats--they're about the survival of the republic.
Chris tried to lighten it up by picking a pizza fight. He's a Chicago deep-dish guy; I'm strictly New York slice. I told him deep-dish is lasagna with PR. He laughed, but I could see the pain behind his eyes.

* * *
We ended where I always like to end: hope. Real, stubborn hope. The kind **Gretchen Whitmer** , **Andy Beshear** , and **Mallory McMorrow** embody every time they show up, speak plainly, and refuse to back down.
Authenticity and courage still win--if we're willing to fight like we mean it. And hey, another guy to check out? [Michigan Lieutenant Governor Garlin Gilchrist, running to be Governor in 2026--we had him on Amped Up yesterday](https://substack.com/redirect/5689a617-0ac0-4489-9c6c-b255213a8862?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We showed how Garlin is out there fighting like a real leader right now--[kind of like this guy, who I wrote about just two days ago](https://substack.com/redirect/af35850b-85a2-44e0-a013-306ef0cc4ab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Newsom has taken his mockery of Trump sycophants to a whole other level.

body:
What is causing these young people to become monsters?

|

| | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zmvnq5sigt0ja1vgokuv90fkbhjkcqolsreocfp8_rp22sh2s8i6eor4c3gm0o36clh2bs) Friend,

The rise in political violence is frightening enough, but once I realized the truth behind the terror, it chilled me to the very core of my being.

These terrorists aren’t who you’d expect. They are young people who come from ordinary, middle-class families, living in functional homes with loving parents.

_**What is causing these young people to become monsters?**_

A growing nihilistic online culture — that believes life is meaningless, truth is subjective, and nothing ultimately matters — seeks to tear down and destroy all that is good in our society.

This destructive philosophy is seeping into American households through memes, message boards, comment sections, and peer-to-peer apps – undetected by parents, law enforcement, and society at large.

_**How can you and I reverse this worrisome trend? **_

In her address to the graduating class of West Point, Ayn Rand gave us a clue:

“Observe young people's dread of independence...When men abandon reason, they find not only that their emotions cannot guide them, but that they can experience no emotions save one: terror.”

Like cornered animals, they turn and seek to inflict terror on others.

The remedy is simple: A return to REASON. By introducing the rising generation to the ideas of Ayn Rand, we can counter the terrifying nihilism gripping young people today.

I’m Jennifer Anju Grossman, CEO of The Atlas Society. Our mission is to inspire people to embrace reason, achievement, benevolence, and rational self-interest as the moral foundation for political liberty, personal happiness, and a flourishing society.

**Through our viral videos, podcasts, graphic novels, online courses, and live events, we reach the next generation where they get their information and give them the tools to reject the brutality, despair, and irrationalism they absorb online.**

[You can help us end the chaos and misery that is gripping our young people and our society by donating today.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z8jj5mo5lufcmi8je9j4esar62rgfc9jcljmfogg_rp22sh2s8i6eor4c3gm0o36clh2bs)

Online nihilism isn’t just a fringe meme; it’s a cultural force.

It disarms individuals, weakens societies, and undermines the very foundations that allow civilizations to thrive.

This nihilism doesn’t just reflect despair; it shapes behavior, attitudes, and even politics in deeply consequential ways.

And we’ve all seen the terrible consequences played out before our very eyes... The assassination of Charlie Kirk is just one tragic example.

Young people are desperate for meaning, purpose, and acceptance. And if they fail to find meaning, they reject everything and fill that void with radical ideologies.

**They need heroes who inspire them to achieve greatness and a philosophy that guides them to embrace reason, facts, and debate – rather than violence.**

That’s why The Atlas Society leverages content that young audiences gravitate towards, such as our action-packed animated book trailers, provocative "Draw My Life" videos, and captivating graphic novels.

clean_body: What is causing these young people to become monsters? | | | Friend, The rise in political violence is frightening enough, but once I realized the truth behind the terror, it chilled me to the very core of my being. These terrorists aren’t who you’d expect. They are young people who come from ordinary, middle-class families, living in functional homes with loving parents. What is causing these young people to become monsters? A growing nihilistic online culture — that believes life is meaningless, truth is subjective, and nothing ultimately matters — seeks to tear down and destroy all that is good in our society. This destructive philosophy is seeping into American households through memes, message boards, comment sections, and peer-to-peer apps – undetected by parents, law enforcement, and society at large. How can you and I reverse this worrisome trend? In her address to the graduating class of West Point, Ayn Rand gave us a clue: “Observe young people's dread of independence...When men abandon reason, they find not only that their emotions cannot guide them, but that they can experience no emotions save one: terror.” Like cornered animals, they turn and seek to inflict terror on others. The remedy is simple: A return to REASON. By introducing the rising generation to the ideas of Ayn Rand, we can counter the terrifying nihilism gripping young people today. I’m Jennifer Anju Grossman, CEO of The Atlas Society. Our mission is to inspire people to embrace reason, achievement, benevolence, and rational self-interest as the moral foundation for political liberty, personal happiness, and a flourishing society. Through our viral videos, podcasts, graphic novels, online courses, and live events, we reach the next generation where they get their information and give them the tools to reject the brutality, despair, and irrationalism they absorb online. Online nihilism isn’t just a fringe meme; it’s a cultural force. It disarms individuals, weakens societies, and undermines the very foundations that allow civilizations to thrive. This nihilism doesn’t just reflect despair; it shapes behavior, attitudes, and even politics in deeply consequential ways. And we’ve all seen the terrible consequences played out before our very eyes... The assassination of Charlie Kirk is just one tragic example. Young people are desperate for meaning, purpose, and acceptance. And if they fail to find meaning, they reject everything and fill that void with radical ideologies. They need heroes who inspire them to achieve greatness and a philosophy that guides them to embrace reason, facts, and debate – rather than violence. That’s why The Atlas Society leverages content that young audiences gravitate towards, such as our action-packed animated book trailers, provocative "Draw My Life" videos, and captivating graphic novels. By introducing the next generation to the empowering principles of Objectivism, we provide a rational and moral alternative to the violent culture of nihilism. We provide hope. But we can’t do it without your help. Thank you for helping us fight back. Jennifer Anju Grossman (JAG) CEO, The Atlas Society P.S. The battle for the future isn’t just political — it’s philosophical. And right now, it’s being waged in the minds of young people online. The Atlas Society is fighting fire with fire, or better yet, memes with memes. But we do so much more than that. We’re showing the next generation that life does have meaning and that they have the power to shape their own destiny. The Atlas Society is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. I have some absolutely incredible news: For the second consecutive filing period, we have outraised our opponent!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us9.campaign-archive.com/?e=606d7e9aa2&u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=970d79773a)

| |

Friend,
I have some absolutely incredible news: [**For the second consecutive filing period, we have outraised our opponent!**](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=c43fe4bb46&e=606d7e9aa2)**** We raised **$12,795** from **82 contributors** , while our opponent raised **$8,198** from only **12 contributors.**
When we launched this campaign, **the political establishment wrote us off**. They looked at our opponent's war chest and the endless special interest money flowing their way and **declared this race over before it even began**. They said we couldn’t compete. They said we couldn’t build a grassroots movement strong enough to challenge that kind of power.
Thanks to dedicated supporters like you making small-dollar donations, we didn't just keep pace, we surged past them again. Honestly, **we should not be in this good of a position** right now. This is a testament to the fact that people power still matters.

### Now for the Final Push: GOTV
###
This financial victory is thrilling, but it's only a momentum builder. We can’t allow this hard work and these historic wins to stop short of the finish line.
The final, most critical step is **Get Out The Vote (GOTV)**. This is how we staff our phone banks, launch our final canvassing blitzes, and make sure every single person who believes in our movement actually casts a ballot. This is how we convert momentum into victory.
[We are currently **$2,358 short** of fully funding that crucial GOTV operation.](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=348d08319e&e=606d7e9aa2)
That is a small gap for such a massive goal. Just **$2,358** is all that stands between us and ensuring we have the resources needed to mobilize our community and secure our win on Election Day.
[If you can chip in $5, $25, or whatever you can afford, we can close this small deficit today and launch our final, game-changing push.](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=59780f2f8b&e=606d7e9aa2)
---

---
| |
We’ve proven that we are the **stronger, smarter, and more dedicated campaign**. Let's not let a small funding gap keep us from securing the victory we’ve fought so hard for.
Thank you for believing in what we can achieve together!
In Solidarity,
Dr. Gary P. MillerDemocratic NomineeHouse of Delegates 49

WelcomeFest featured some _interesting_ takes, [most notably where guests said they believed unions were the most significant detriment to the Abundance Agenda](https://substack.com/redirect/06a8ae11-c6f4-4fe5-861c-4f724bbae88d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- confirming what many feared about the anti-labor sentiments behind it -- and included a who's who of centrist, moderate Congresspeople.

According to authors Simon Bazelon, Lauren Harper Pope, and Liam Kerr, _Deciding to Win_ "aims to provide the most comprehensive account to date of why Democrats lost and what our party needs to do to win again." They claim to draw on hundreds of polls and academic papers, dozens of case studies, and 500,000 survey responses to compile their findings to "give ourselves the best chance to win."
They recommended **five changes** Democrats should make:
1️⃣ Focus on an economic agenda centered on lowering costs, growing the economy, creating jobs, and expanding the social safety net.
2️⃣ Advocate for _popular_ economic policies (drug price negotiation, making the wealthy pay their fair share, $15 minimum wage) rather than _unpopular_ ones (student loan forgiveness, EV subsidies, Medicare for All).
3️⃣ Convince voters we share their priorities -- the economy, cost of living, health care, border security, public safety -- and focus less on issues voters think we emphasize too much (climate change, democracy, abortion, identity and cultural issues).
4️⃣ Moderate positions on immigration, public safety, energy production, and identity/culture issues.
5️⃣ Criticize the outsized influence of corporations and the ultra-wealthy -- but without sounding like socialists.
I have to admit, I went into this already biased -- expecting repurposed Third Way takes and a condescending chastising of progressive politics. But I dug in anyway because I'm interested in an **all-of-the-above approach** to winning on the Left. So -- like many of you -- I have thoughts. Here's what they got right and what they got wrong.
Credit where credit is due. The authors make some excellent points -- many of which I _do_ agree with.
**Focusing our policy agenda on economic growth and opportunity** is essential if we want to win back working-class Americans again. Expanding prescription drug negotiation, making the wealthy pay their fair share, raising the minimum wage to $15 an hour -- all extremely popular and entirely achievable.
But here's the real issue:
Democrats have _talked_ about these things for years... **just too cautiously and too conservatively**. We nibble around the edges. We propose half-measures. We water down the bold ideas that would actually close the obscene wealth gap in this country.
As I wrote previously: **the blueprint exists** -- FDR's New Deal, labor-forward populism, economic justice -- but we've spent too long governing like we're still terrified of Ronald Reagan's ghost.
The report also correctly points out something that should ring in every strategist's ears:
> Most voters think Democrats **don 't share their priorities**.
And that's not because we don't care -- it's because we spend so much time reacting to Republican cultural attacks that we **bury** our strongest message: "We want you to thrive."
But this isn't black-and-white.
We can walk and chew gum at the same time.
**We don 't need to throw LGBTQ+ people under the bus just to talk about inflation.** We **don 't** need to sacrifice immigrant communities to show we care about the economy. We **don 't** need to pretend public safety and racial justice are mutually exclusive.
We _can_ lead with affordability and wages and still **stand proudly in our values**. The authors say we should defend our morals -- and they're right! But then they turn around and imply we should mute those morals whenever the polling dips. That's not courage. That's fear.
Another point where they're spot-on:
**Corporate power is rotting our democracy from the inside out.
** Money has warped policy outcomes against working people for decades.
But the report badly misinterprets what that means. Wealthy donors don't drive progressive policies -- they're driven by **popular demand**. Billionaires didn't invent movements like the Fight for $15; workers won them.
Finally -- _hallelujah_ -- the authors admit Democrats rely too heavily on **old-guard consultants** and message-tested political Mad Libs. We keep falling for the Magic Word Fallacy -- believing there's some perfect sentence that will unlock the electorate.
Meanwhile, Republicans are:
✅ Dominating digital
✅ Setting the agenda
✅ Taking risks
✅ Investing everywhere
Democrats need to be **bolder** , **faster** , and **less afraid** of new tactics -- not hiding behind the Clinton-era playbook like it's sacred scripture.
Bold ideas + bold messaging = winning energy.
Timid ideas + timid messaging = "Why bother voting?"
On the whole, Welcome _does_ name the right challenges. But they still prescribe the **same cautious centrism** that keeps causing them.
## **❌ What It Gets Wrong**
Okay, now that we've given them credit, let's talk about where the analysis... falls apart.
First, and this is a big one: **they only looked at voters**. Like, literally only the people who already participate in elections. What about the **one-third of the country** that didn't vote last year? Tens of millions of Americans -- many of whom are working class -- didn't show up because they believe politics doesn't help them. They see Congress spend billions on foreign aid, while they struggle to afford groceries, rent, child care, and healthcare. They are not "lazy nonvoters." They're people who feel the government has failed them. If we want to expand the electorate, we need to understand what will bring _them_ back into the fold -- not just cater to those who already show up.
**And then there 's the claim that Democrats have "moved too far Left."** I'm sorry, but... have they looked around? The Overton window has shifted. Issues once deemed "radical" -- like marriage equality -- are now standard Democratic Party planks. **Progress is not extremism.** Support for LGBTQ+ rights is up. Support for abortion rights surged post-Dobbs. Labor organizing is at its most popular point in decades. Americans aren't recoiling at progressive values -- they're frustrated that Democrats aren't fighting hard enough for them.
**The report also oversimplifies some incredibly complicated issues.** Just saying "immigration" doesn't capture the nuance of what voters believe. Most people support legal immigration and don't think families should be torn apart. They're mad that the system is broken, not that immigrants exist--same thing with student debt. People don't hate debt relief because they hate students -- they hate that the system got so predatory that millions were forced into lifelong financial crisis just to pursue higher education.
And here's the big messaging failure they ignore: **priority isn 't the same as popularity**. Just because voters rank cost of living above climate change doesn't mean climate isn't important to them. It just means **rent is due on the first of every month,** while sea level rise feels abstract by comparison. We need to be able to walk and chew gum.
**Which leads to another glaring issue: they seriously underestimate media distortion and the gap between perception and reality.** If all you ever hear about Democrats is from Fox News, far-right influencers, and conspiracy-driven Facebook groups calling us "anti-American Marxists," then yes -- you might think Democrats don't share your values. Biden didn't become unpopular because his policies were unpopular -- he became unpopular because he never effectively countered the constant right-wing messaging machine.
This goes beyond candidates and labels. It includes policies and ideas as well.
"Socialism" is an evil, dirty form of government that sinks foreign corrupt countries and was what the Nazis were trying to enact, according to what people are told and spew on the internet. To them, it's anti-American, but those same people still wouldn't want to overpay to use privatized roads, emergency services, schools, or any other public service that stems from socialist ideas. They fully embrace the freedom that those public services give them.
"Medicare for All" is communism that will make everyone sick and overcrowd our hospitals. But those same people want to be able to receive medical care without going into debt and embrace the idea of free preventative care during times of epidemics.
"Regulation" prevents growth that only a free market can provide. Yet all these same people still lose their minds when prices go up at the grocery store and want to know what the government is doing about it.
That is not the same as "Democrats went too far left." It's a **communications war we keep losing**.
**They also ignore the "Democratic Penalty" entirely. **In red-leaning states, having a "D" next to your name is sometimes the kiss of death -- even if your policies are popular. We've seen it repeatedly: Sherrod Brown, Jon Tester, Heidi Heitkamp... Candidates who should've been a natural fit for working-class voters -- but lost or nearly lost because the brand has been successfully demonized.
What it means is that Democrats need to build more organizational power in these areas and ensure they are visible in everyday life to refute those claims. **It 's easier for someone to vilify a stranger than to demonize a neighbor.**
**And please -- the perfect-candidate mythology has to die. **The authors list a bunch of centrist Democrats they think we should replicate everywhere -- but AOC can't win in rural Washington, and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez can't win in the Bronx. The country is not a monolith. People vote for someone they **know** , someone who shows up, someone who listens. We need more people who look like, talk like, and live like the people they want to represent from their communities. Not a poll-tested Frankenstein candidate engineered and parachuted in from a D.C. lab.
**Finally, on money in politics, they are right that voters hate the corrupting influence of wealthy elites.** But then they bizarrely imply that progressive ideas are only popular _because_ big donors fund them -- which is just not true. Billionaires didn't build movements like union power, racial justice, and reproductive freedom. They were built by **people organizing**. Meanwhile, corporate interests have spent decades rigging the economy against workers -- and Republicans have successfully branded _us_ as the out-of-touch elitists. If Democrats want to reclaim economic populism, we should be pointing out who's actually hoarding wealth and rigging the rules.
**✅ To sum it up:**
**The problem isn 't that Democrats are too progressive.**
**The problem is that Democrats sometimes sound like they don 't believe in their own agenda.**
**We don 't lose because we fight for too much.**
**We lose because we fight for too little -- and let Republicans define us.**
## **✅ Conclusion: Bold or Bust**
So while I commend the authors of _Deciding-to-win_ on what they are trying to do, there is much left to be desired -- and this feels very much like running to the middle and punching left again. And that has never worked, especially not last year for Vice President Harris.
Because here's the truth: **America isn 't asking for smaller dreams**. They're asking for leaders who will fight like hell for them -- not for shareholders or lobbyists or whatever consultant said the "safe" thing polls best with suburban dads.
We can't fix a system that's rigged against working people by nibbling around the edges. We can't build a multiracial working-class coalition by telling parts of that coalition to sit quietly in the back. We can't win back trust by sounding like we're afraid of our own values.
Democrats must lead with conviction -- not apology.
We win when:
* We **name who 's screwing people over** (corporate landlords, private equity, price-gouging monopolies)
* We **fight for broad, visible improvements** in people's daily lives (lower costs, higher wages, good housing, safe communities)
* We **show up everywhere** , not just where it's comfortable
* We **expand the electorate** , not just chase the fraction who already vote

We are the party that built Social Security, Medicare, the 40-hour work week, the Civil Rights Act, marriage equality, and the first major climate legislation in history. That's not "too left." That's **popular**. That's **the majority**. That's **winning**.
So yes, Democrats need to be bolder in their approaches and braver in their fights -- and that doesn't mean retreating to old habits of centrist, moderate politics. It means remembering who we are at our best: the party that **takes on entrenched power and delivers for working people**.
Not a party trying to squeeze into whatever polling box the consultants drew up this week.
If we choose boldness, clarity, and economic justice, we can build a coalition big enough to win -- and win big.
If we don't?
Well, the authors of _Deciding to Win_ already gave us the title of the sequel:
**Choosing-to-Lose.**

Which leads to another glaring issue: they seriously underestimate media distortion and the gap between perception and reality. If all you ever hear about Democrats is from Fox News, far-right influencers, and conspiracy-driven Facebook groups calling us "anti-American Marxists," then yes -- you might think Democrats don't share your values. Biden didn't become unpopular because his policies were unpopular -- he became unpopular because he never effectively countered the constant right-wing messaging machine. This goes beyond candidates and labels. It includes policies and ideas as well. "Socialism" is an evil, dirty form of government that sinks foreign corrupt countries and was what the Nazis were trying to enact, according to what people are told and spew on the internet. To them, it's anti-American, but those same people still wouldn't want to overpay to use privatized roads, emergency services, schools, or any other public service that stems from socialist ideas. They fully embrace the freedom that those public services give them. "Medicare for All" is communism that will make everyone sick and overcrowd our hospitals. But those same people want to be able to receive medical care without going into debt and embrace the idea of free preventative care during times of epidemics. "Regulation" prevents growth that only a free market can provide. Yet all these same people still lose their minds when prices go up at the grocery store and want to know what the government is doing about it. That is not the same as "Democrats went too far left." It's a communications war we keep losing. They also ignore the "Democratic Penalty" entirely. In red-leaning states, having a "D" next to your name is sometimes the kiss of death -- even if your policies are popular. We've seen it repeatedly: Sherrod Brown, Jon Tester, Heidi Heitkamp... Candidates who should've been a natural fit for working-class voters -- but lost or nearly lost because the brand has been successfully demonized. What it means is that Democrats need to build more organizational power in these areas and ensure they are visible in everyday life to refute those claims. It 's easier for someone to vilify a stranger than to demonize a neighbor. And please -- the perfect-candidate mythology has to die. The authors list a bunch of centrist Democrats they think we should replicate everywhere -- but AOC can't win in rural Washington, and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez can't win in the Bronx. The country is not a monolith. People vote for someone they know , someone who shows up, someone who listens. We need more people who look like, talk like, and live like the people they want to represent from their communities. Not a poll-tested Frankenstein candidate engineered and parachuted in from a D.C. lab. Finally, on money in politics, they are right that voters hate the corrupting influence of wealthy elites. But then they bizarrely imply that progressive ideas are only popular because big donors fund them -- which is just not true. Billionaires didn't build movements like union power, racial justice, and reproductive freedom. They were built by people organizing. Meanwhile, corporate interests have spent decades rigging the economy against workers -- and Republicans have successfully branded us as the out-of-touch elitists. If Democrats want to reclaim economic populism, we should be pointing out who's actually hoarding wealth and rigging the rules. ✅ To sum it up: The problem isn 't that Democrats are too progressive. The problem is that Democrats sometimes sound like they don 't believe in their own agenda. We don 't lose because we fight for too much. We lose because we fight for too little -- and let Republicans define us. ✅ Conclusion: Bold or Bust So while I commend the authors of Deciding-to-win on what they are trying to do, there is much left to be desired -- and this feels very much like running to the middle and punching left again. And that has never worked, especially not last year for Vice President Harris. Because here's the truth: America isn 't asking for smaller dreams. They're asking for leaders who will fight like hell for them -- not for shareholders or lobbyists or whatever consultant said the "safe" thing polls best with suburban dads. We can't fix a system that's rigged against working people by nibbling around the edges. We can't build a multiracial working-class coalition by telling parts of that coalition to sit quietly in the back. We can't win back trust by sounding like we're afraid of our own values. Democrats must lead with conviction -- not apology. We win when: We name who 's screwing people over (corporate landlords, private equity, price-gouging monopolies) We fight for broad, visible improvements in people's daily lives (lower costs, higher wages, good housing, safe communities) We show up everywhere , not just where it's comfortable We expand the electorate , not just chase the fraction who already vote We are the party that built Social Security, Medicare, the 40-hour work week, the Civil Rights Act, marriage equality, and the first major climate legislation in history. That's not "too left." That's popular. That's the majority. That's winning. So yes, Democrats need to be bolder in their approaches and braver in their fights -- and that doesn't mean retreating to old habits of centrist, moderate politics. It means remembering who we are at our best: the party that takes on entrenched power and delivers for working people. Not a party trying to squeeze into whatever polling box the consultants drew up this week. If we choose boldness, clarity, and economic justice, we can build a coalition big enough to win -- and win big. If we don't? Well, the authors of Deciding to Win already gave us the title of the sequel: Choosing-to-Lose. As always, thank you for reading By the Ballot. Please remember to like, subscribe, and share on Substack, Spotify, YouTube, Apple Podcasts, or wherever you get your podcasts. We're also up on now if that's your sort of thing to get more content from us. We will be back next week, one final time ahead of the Elections on Tuesday, November 4th, with our closing argument to the 2025 cycle. So tune in and we'll see y'all there. By the Ballot is a free SubStack that features unapologetic dispatches from the New South 's next generation of Democrats. Commentary on stances, tactics, and news on the Left. We don't claim to know everything or always be right, we just want to be a part of the conversation. While there 's many different ways to power and the Right wants to take over our country by hook or by crook, we want to help Democrats help Americans by making a government for the people by the ballot. | Peter,
Sometimes voting can not only be satisfying, it can feel downright incredible.
In the midst of so much negativity, bad news, and Trump's daily stream of lies and insanity--there is joy in simple yet powerful acts of defiance and self-expression.
And on Tuesday, voters in Pennsylvania get to channel all of these frustrations into action: three Democratic justices on the state Supreme Court are up for retention, and MAGA has made it their mission to "knock out" all three of them, unwinding the 5-2 Dem majority on the court in a single election.
The joy of politics is in coming together to make change, to speak with one voice, and to fight for what's right...and it can be infectious.

### China's clean energy revolution demonstrates what we could have had decades ago

---

The year is 1988, and the United States is on the cusp of a renewable energy revolution. Lithium batteries, electric motors, and photovoltaic solar panels were all invented here; 85 percent of the world's solar market was based in the U.S. And there was bipartisan political will to begin prioritizing non-fossil fuel energy sources. "Those who think we are powerless to do anything about the greenhouse effect forget about the 'White House effect,'" George H. W. Bush [said](https://substack.com/redirect/658b674c-acfb-4f75-9455-90e8753afb49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a campaign speech after becoming the Republican nominee for president. "In my first year in office, I will convene a global conference on the environment at the White House. It will include the Soviets, the Chinese. ... The agenda will be clear. We will talk about global warming."
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE3NzUyNjY4NCwicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc2MTgzMDY3OSwiZXhwIjoyMDc3NDA2Njc5LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.HORqmieiI6tVdc_6jhCVTz2whZSz3l-5ZmiI96PVXSY?)
The notion then was that the U.S. would have to drag China into cooperating. At that time, renewable energy was essentially nonexistent in China. In fact, the Communist government did not articulate clear goals for expanding its domestic clean energy industry until the release of its Twelfth Five-Year Plan, in 2010, when for the first time it [identified](https://substack.com/redirect/20d769a2-cfbb-4091-ba8f-ea3fd1b34c50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the fight against climate change as a major challenge. That year, China had [significantly less](https://substack.com/redirect/b89c8c56-e75a-497f-878e-57eee37e2015?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) combined wind and solar capacity than the U.S.
Just a decade and a half later, China is [manufacturing](https://substack.com/redirect/0b7e4c52-cc58-41cf-a3d2-95508099c9e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 92 percent of the world's solar panels, 82 percent of the world's wind turbines, and [three-quarters](https://substack.com/redirect/d07ef5aa-3ac3-4c62-9fd2-8f2e7fce78e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the world's batteries. This dominance has dramatically reduced costs--Chinese solar panel prices dropped 40 percent in 2023 alone, and China's BYD, the [world's largest](https://substack.com/redirect/8871b7b1-4c6a-4816-8e00-124e08170eb3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) EV manufacturer, now sells high-quality EVs for just $10,000--and sparked a clean energy explosion across the globe. It took from 1954 to 2022 for humanity to install one terawatt of solar capacity. Just two years later, in 2024, the world hit two terawatts. Pakistan went from basically zero solar capacity to 25 percent of all its electricity coming from solar in just a few years, with solar panel imports from China doubling between 2023 and 2024. Algeria imported 630 times more Chinese solar panels in the first half of 2025 than it had in 2024.
So it took less than 15 years for one global power (and not even the wealthiest or most technologically advanced one) to create a global energy market in which renewables are outcompeting fossil fuels, despite the [trillions of dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/a15df690-fdf8-4245-a1a1-5bc25d8ec272?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in economic and political subsidies that continue to structurally advantage oil and gas in profound ways. Meanwhile, 37 years after it seemed poised to dominate the clean energy transition, the U.S. has become a full-on petrostate.
So what happened?
### **The Conspiracy**
Here is where we see the most significant independent variable in the comparison between the U.S. and China--the response of their respective fossil fuel industries. Unlike China's state-run coal companies, which never attacked climate science, in the U.S., Big Oil began implementing a massive scheme to poison the public with climate denial in order to, as one 1988 internal Exxon [memo](https://substack.com/redirect/e7c4fb65-d475-4bbf-a426-7af0031f06ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) put it, block the "development of nonfossil fuel resources."
And that's just what they did.
In 1991, a group of fossil fuel companies founded the [Information Council on the Environment](https://substack.com/redirect/a9ba3473-28f6-470a-b9d1-a33f56e3921c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to "Reposition global warming as theory (not fact)." ICE conducted polling that found that 80 percent of Americans thought that the problem of climate change was serious. To dismantle this consensus, ICE planned to target "not typically active information-seekers" with climate denying radio commercials, public relations tours, mailers, and newspaper advertisements featuring messages like, "Who told you the Earth was warming... Chicken Little?"
In 1998, representatives from major fossil fuel companies produced the "[Global Climate Science Communications Action Plan](https://substack.com/redirect/37141a75-d053-478d-ba29-5bfb79979367?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," which outlined a multimillion-dollar campaign to make climate denial "part of the 'conventional wisdom'" and laid out a series of strategies designed to flood Americans with false claims that there was no scientific consensus about the reality of climate change. These tactics included buying off "independent" scientists to spread climate denial, "advertising the scientific uncertainties" in various markets, and distributing their propaganda "directly to schools"--all tactics the fossil fuel industry went on to execute in the United States and across Europe.
### **Legal Accountability**
Today, this decades-long campaign to fraudulently turn the public against climate action is the subject of dozens of lawsuits against oil companies by plaintiffs seeking damages for climate harms. These suits have great promise. But they also face [massive obstacles](https://substack.com/redirect/ad42307a-9261-4fc1-a518-8e51a20e133f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), as you'd expect when taking on the most powerful corporations in the world.
One of the top arguments the fossil fuel industry has used to try to evade accountability for their fraud relates to causation. To hold a defendant liable for misconduct, a plaintiff has to demonstrate that the defendant's actions were a substantial factor in causing harm to the plaintiff. Big Oil's army of lawyers are quick to claim that, even if the fossil fuel industry did lie about climate change, plaintiffs cannot prove that these lies necessarily played a substantial role in driving climate damages.
There are different ways to try to demonstrate the causal impact of Big Oil's deception. You can compare the actual scientific consensus on climate with the public's perception of that consensus. The most recent [analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/a1521561-d65e-4ad7-9fb8-b3c4f126d2ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the peer-reviewed scientific literature found that there is greater than 99 percent agreement on the existence and causes of man-made climate change, yet a 2015 Yale-George Mason University [poll](https://substack.com/redirect/9a993aa1-2628-49ea-b835-b7310e5a259f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that only one in ten Americans understands this. As the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) [noted](https://substack.com/redirect/ce5224c8-3f64-4c1d-a89d-0a2a2f7bef46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in its sixth assessment report, "misinformation and politicization of climate change science has created polarization in public and policy domains in North America, particularly in the US, limiting climate action," which, in turn, "inflates climate risks."
But the recent history of clean energy development in China offers another compelling piece of evidence for this causal link. After all, causation is essentially determined by asking, "What would have happened if the conduct at issue had not occurred?" China provides that counterfactual. On the one hand, we have a superpower, the U.S., that was primed with every advantage to begin developing clean energy economies of scale more than three decades ago, but instead doubled down as a petrostate after its fossil fuel industry fraudulently polarized a substantial portion of its population against climate action. On the other hand, we have China--the one superpower in the world where those western Big Oil companies don't have influence and were not able to poison the well with their deception--which has in just a few years succeeded in remaking the global energy system such that renewables are now cheaper than fossil fuels.
### **Race Against Time**
It's important to note this timescale, because the fight against climate change is fundamentally a race against time. And it's a race that humanity is losing badly, as evidenced by the terrifying recent [determination](https://substack.com/redirect/900516be-7b9c-4ac4-9345-58e2e44fbab4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Earth has reached its first catastrophic climate tipping point--coral reefs have entered terminal decline, condemning vast swathes of the planet's biodiversity and the livelihoods of hundreds of millions--and is on the brink of several others, including the destruction of the Amazon, the collapse of global ocean currents, and the loss of polar ice sheets.
The speed of the world's renewable energy explosion following the prioritization of clean energy by a single global power proves that this dystopian timeline was far from inevitable. Absent Big Oil's climate fraud, it is likely that the West could have achieved these clean energy milestones decades earlier, giving humanity more than enough time to transition off of fossil fuels before we hit the apocalyptic tipping points we are currently hurtling towards. In other words, Big Oil's lies did cause--or at the very least were a substantial factor in causing--the catastrophic climate harms we are experiencing today.
Of course, no historical counterfactual can be absolutely definitive. There are obviously many differences between the U.S. in the 1990s and China in the 2010s beyond the presence or absence of fossil fuel-funded campaigns of climate deception. But none of these differences strongly cut against the causation analysis. For example, you could argue that China, with its system of state control, could direct resources toward clean energy in a way the U.S. never could have. But the U.S. can clearly marshal vast resources for its priorities (think of the interstate highway system, the Apollo program, or the development of AI data centers) and had far more resources to marshal; in 2010, when China began its renewables buildout, its GDP was just over one third that of the U.S.
You could also argue that it's just not possible to compare what might have happened in the democratic U.S. to what did occur in the single-party autocracy of China. But the evidence does not indicate that a more democratic China, kept free of Big Oil's propaganda, would have been less supportive of a clean energy buildout. Indeed, [peer-reviewed national survey data](https://substack.com/redirect/94a64a27-bcb1-4be8-9ac4-aec3980da98d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on public demand for climate action finds that while the U.S. ranks at the bottom of the international list, China--the country that western Big Oil companies have had the least ability to influence--is right up at the top, with 97 percent supporting demands for greater political action on climate.
### **What They Stole From Us**
I don't know whether this argument will ever be used in a court of law. But every time you hear a piece of good news about the explosive growth of clean energy, it's worth remembering that the benchmark in question likely could have been met in 2005, rather than 2025, if not for Big Oil's climate deception. Every time you hear bad news about another catastrophic wildfire, drought, heat wave, or storm, or the nightmarish arrival of another cataclysmic climate tipping point, remember that we could have had 20 more years to address this crisis had Big Oil not stopped the West from taking earlier action.
Fossil fuel companies, in order to maintain their garish profits--and Big Oil executives, in order to buy their fourth homes and private jets and, increasingly, [luxury bunkers](https://substack.com/redirect/0c8ce785-560e-4f51-a0ac-c1f33feff317?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--knowingly stole humanity's best chance to address climate change on a timeline that would have averted apocalypse. It's the most despicable crime in the history of our species. Hopefully human civilization can survive long enough for some measure of justice to be exacted against the scoundrels responsible.
